stem: Under the contract described, how did the sharecropper pay for the use of the land?

options.text: With cash wages paid weekly by the landowner
With a share of the year’s crop
With a fixed yearly rent paid in advance
options.misconception: Sharecropping means paying a fixed cash rent.

options.text: By giving the landowner a portion of his tools
options.misconception: The worker paid rent with his tools.

rationales.A: No wages appear in the contract; the worker is paid in crop, not cash.
rationales.B: The contract says it plainly: the freedmen “receive one-half of the crop after the debts for supplies are paid.” The crop itself is the rent.
rationales.C: Background: A fixed cash rent describes tenant farming, a step above sharecropping.
rationales.D: The landowner furnishes the tools; the worker does not pay with them.
rationales.general:
1. Find the payment. The contract names it: one-half of the crop.
2. Ask what that means. The worker has no cash wage; the harvest is his pay and his rent in one.
3. Test the other payments. No weekly wages, no cash rent, and no payment in tools appear.
4. Match the system. Paying rent with a share of the crop is what makes this sharecropping.
Remember: the name of the system is the payment — a share of the crop.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrased from sharecropping contracts of the period, including the De Soto County, Mississippi, contract of 1867 (Salisbury University, Nabb Research Center). Image: title page of the 1867 De Soto County contract.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of a sharecropping contract, De Soto County, Mississippi, 1867. The freedmen agree to work the landowner’s plantation for one year. The landowner furnishes the land, seed, tools, and housing. The freedmen receive one-half of the crop after the debts for supplies are paid. Supplies are bought on credit from the landowner, and the crop stands as security for the debt.

source: original; stimulus paraphrases sharecropping contracts of the period, with the title page of the 1867 De Soto County contract
